Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically unless you finish with SELECT <successful step> to choose an
already executed build. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

Working procedure:
1. Record a compact visible-object inventory, including cropped foreground objects, and
   several approximate image landmarks across foreground, subject and background. Image
   coordinates estimated by eye are estimates, not measured calibration. Choose a coherent
   world scale; absolute size and camera distance are not identifiable from this image alone.
2. Parameterize camera pose, focal length and shift separately from object dimensions.
   Use room edge directions, verticals, visible top surfaces and depth-dependent size ratios
   to estimate viewpoint. Compare global framing against local silhouette disagreement.
   A focal change changes framing throughout the view; translation also changes parallax.
   Do not compensate for local shape errors by scaling the whole scene or camera together.
3. Build a complete economical scene first, with semantic Asset groups, explicit supports,
   major colors and distinctive outlines. Include visible peripheral objects before dense
   textures, stitches or repeated ornaments. Keep all parts of a movable object in its
   hierarchy, so a parent edit moves its upholstery, trim, legs and attachments together.
4. Derive contact heights from supporting geometry and use explicit anchors or bind where
   appropriate. Check contact after rotation or resizing. World AABB contact is approximate:
   curved surfaces and overlapping components require geometric interpretation. Do not
   treat intended intersections within a constructed part as physical collision failures.
5. Before execution, audit all API preconditions below. After a successful render, identify
   the largest visible disagreement and revise one main parameter family at a time. Check
   unrelated landmarks and support relations after the change. Preserve successful geometry
   during error repair. Missing render output is a failure, not visual evidence.
6. For an apparently missing object, check construction, unique inclusion keys, hierarchy,
   camera framing and intervening surfaces before adding a duplicate or enlarging it.
   Presence in a graph does not prove visibility. Absence from a truncated report does not
   prove omission. Do not infer whole-object scale from a probe on a decorative subpart.

Implementation checks grounded in the fixed API:
- All primitive dimensions and radii must be finite and positive. fillet_box requires
  0 < radius <= min(size)/2. For a thin object needing broad planar rounding, compose
  suitable primitives rather than increasing the fillet radius past this limit.
- Rod endpoints must differ; consecutive sweep_tube points must differ.
- include replaces an existing sibling with the same key. Use unique indexed keys in loops.
  It returns the attached node, which can be a clone; retain that returned reference.
- Layout functions and snap return copies. Attach the returned copy before binding it.
- Bind endpoints must already belong to the scene, cannot be ancestor/descendant, and
  dependencies must be acyclic. Supply source_anchor and target_anchor explicitly.
- realize clears Blender. Set camera, lights and bpy materials afterward. If customizing
  the world, first create and assign bpy.data.worlds.new('World') when scene.world is None,
  then enable use_nodes before accessing shader nodes.
- Semantic inclusion keys name Blender EMPTY markers; primitive mesh children may retain
  names such as Box or Rod. Apply material edits through the semantic group's descendants,
  not a presumed mesh name. Copy shared materials before object-specific modifications.
- Keep construction bounded. Procedural material patterns can represent fine surface detail
  without thousands of separate meshes. Do not change the runner's resource limits.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
The snap and bind calls above explicitly request bottom-to-top placement; their actual
source_anchor defaults are 'center', so do not omit anchors when expressing support.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)

```python
from sceneact import *
import bpy, math, random
from mathutils import Vector

random.seed(14)
scene = Scene('Historic dormitory')

# Observations: dark iron bunks fill the left half; an open oak locker and
# stone fireplace stand on the yellow rear wall. A very close bunk crops right.
# Estimated landmarks: locker (307,174), hearth (401,192), main post (145,202).
# Camera distance and room depth are uncertain; dimensions use a coherent metre scale.
wood = (.25,.125,.052)
iron = (.085,.105,.102)
linen = (.88,.89,.84)
plaster = (.66,.66,.38)
stone = (.38,.36,.29)

def B(parent, key, size, center, color):
    return parent.include(key, box(size=size, center=center, color=color))

def R(parent, key, start, end, radius=.022, color=iron):
    return parent.include(key, rod(radius=radius, start=start, end=end, color=color))

# Architecture builder: individual boards, plaster surfaces and exposed oak frame.
room = Asset('room')
B(room,'floor foundation',(7.2,9,.12),(2.9,.6,-.075),wood)
for i in range(25):
    x=-.65+i*.285
    for j in range(4):
        y=-3.7+j*2.26+((i%3)*.17)
        c=(.28+random.random()*.075,.155+random.random()*.045,.073+random.random()*.025)
        B(room,f'plank_{i}_{j}',(.279,2.247,.035),(x,y,.003),c)
B(room,'left plaster',(.13,8.7,3.05),(-.14,.65,1.525),(.67,.67,.49))
B(room,'rear plaster',(6.6,.15,3.05),(3.1,4.65,1.525),plaster)
B(room,'ceiling',(6.8,8.8,.13),(3.0,.6,3.09),(.66,.68,.47))
for i,y in enumerate([-3.0,-.8,1.5,3.65,4.52]):
    B(room,f'left stud_{i}',(.17,.16,3.03),(-.025,y,1.51),(.16,.12,.065))
for i,z in enumerate([.14,1.05,2.23,2.95]):
    B(room,f'left horizontal_{i}',(.17,8.7,.13),(-.015,.65,z),(.17,.125,.062))
for i,y in enumerate([-.5,3.4]):
    B(room,f'ceiling beam_{i}',(6.6,.22,.23),(3.0,y,2.98),(.12,.095,.046))
scene.include('architecture',room)

# Bunk builder: all frames, mattresses, pillows and ladders share one asset.
def bunk(name,x,y,length=2.13,width=.94):
    a=Asset(name)
    for i,xx in enumerate([x-length/2,x+length/2]):
        for j,yy in enumerate([y-width/2,y+width/2]):
            R(a,f'post_{i}_{j}',(xx,yy,.06),(xx,yy,2.13),.027)
            a.include(f'cap_{i}_{j}',ball(radius=.033,center=(xx,yy,2.135),color=iron))
            B(a,f'foot_{i}_{j}',(.105,.105,.035),(xx,yy,.045),(.21,.22,.19))
    for k,z in enumerate([.46,1.59]):
        B(a,f'bed base_{k}',(length+.025,width,.075),(x,y,z),iron)
        a.include(f'mattress_{k}',fillet_box(size=(length-.035,width-.055,.16),
                  radius=.065,center=(x,y,z+.115),color=linen))
        # White bedding has an overhanging thin edge and a broad folded blanket.
        B(a,f'sheet edge_{k}',(length-.015,width+.018,.052),(x,y,z+.13),(.91,.92,.88))
        a.include(f'duvet_{k}',fillet_box(size=(length*.68,width-.045,.085),
                  radius=.035,center=(x+.27,y,z+.223),color=(.87,.89,.86)))
        a.include(f'pillow_{k}',fillet_box(size=(.47,width*.77,.13),
                  radius=.055,center=(x-length*.35,y,z+.255),color=(.96,.95,.89)))
        for j,yy in enumerate([y-width/2,y+width/2]):
            for n,zz in enumerate([z+.34,z+.49] if k==1 else [z+.23]):
                R(a,f'side rail_{k}_{j}_{n}',(x-length/2,yy,zz),
                  (x+length/2,yy,zz),.018)
        for j,xx in enumerate([x-length/2,x+length/2]):
            for n,zz in enumerate([z+.31,z+.48]):
                R(a,f'end rail_{k}_{j}_{n}',(xx,y-width/2,zz),
                  (xx,y+width/2,zz),.019)
    # Ladder on the end nearest the aisle.
    lx=x+length/2+.025
    for i,yy in enumerate([y-width*.35,y+width*.35]):
        R(a,f'ladder upright_{i}',(lx,yy,.13),(lx,yy,1.98),.021)
    for i in range(6):
        zz=.32+i*.27
        R(a,f'ladder rung_{i}',(lx,y-width*.35,zz),(lx,y+width*.35,zz),.018)
    # Small black, wall-like bed number plate.
    B(a,'number plaque',(.11,.025,.17),(x+length/2-.08,y-width/2-.022,2.08),(.12,.15,.13))
    return a

scene.include('front left bunk',bunk('front left bunk',1.00,.15))
scene.include('rear left bunk',bunk('rear left bunk',1.00,2.28))
# The right-hand foreground object intentionally extends beyond the image.
right=bunk('cropped right bunk',5.05,-1.52,length=2.15,width=.97)
right.turn('z',90,pivot=(5.05,-1.52,0))
scene.include('cropped right bunk',right)

# Locker builder: open right compartment, closed paneled left door, visible hooks.
cab=Asset('oak locker')
cx=2.87
cy=4.34
B(cab,'dark interior',(.92,.09,1.78),(cx,cy+.19,.99),(.105,.063,.025))
for i,x in enumerate([cx-.47,cx+.47]):
    B(cab,f'side_{i}',(.065,.48,1.83),(x,cy,.99),(.30,.16,.059))
B(cab,'divider',(.045,.43,1.76),(cx+.005,cy,.99),(.33,.18,.063))
for i,z in enumerate([.11,.83,1.88]):
    B(cab,f'shelf_{i}',(.97,.52,.065),(cx,cy,z),(.31,.16,.049))
B(cab,'cornice',(1.08,.59,.075),(cx,cy,1.94),(.37,.21,.085))
B(cab,'cornice lip',(1.13,.62,.035),(cx,cy,1.987),(.28,.15,.052))
B(cab,'closed door',(.43,.055,1.70),(cx-.235,cy-.26,.99),(.38,.21,.078))
for i,z in enumerate([.50,1.34]):
    B(cab,f'recessed panel_{i}',(.33,.013,.64),(cx-.235,cy-.294,z),(.31,.155,.047))
    for j,xx in enumerate([cx-.416,cx-.055]):
        B(cab,f'panel stile_{i}_{j}',(.025,.025,.70),(xx,cy-.309,z),(.42,.24,.091))
    for j,zz in enumerate([z-.35,z+.35]):
        B(cab,f'panel rail_{i}_{j}',(.38,.025,.026),(cx-.235,cy-.309,zz),(.42,.24,.091))
for i,x in enumerate([cx-.37,cx+.37]):
    B(cab,f'foot_{i}',(.12,.38,.13),(x,cy,.065),(.24,.12,.036))
for i,z in enumerate([.52,1.30]):
    cab.include(f'door knob_{i}',ball(radius=.018,center=(cx-.08,cy-.335,z),color=(.12,.11,.06)))
for i,x in enumerate([cx+.10,cx+.23,cx+.36]):
    R(cab,f'hook_{i}',(x,cy+.09,1.74),(x,cy-.015,1.69),.012, color=(.12,.11,.08))
scene.include('locker',cab)

# Fireplace builder: a shallow dark recess, individually jointed stone surround.
fire=Asset('stone fireplace')
fx=4.49
fy=4.505
B(fire,'black opening',(1.36,.055,1.17),(fx,fy-.045,.59),(.075,.066,.049))
B(fire,'hearth slab',(1.97,.90,.07),(fx,4.22,.047),(.30,.28,.22))
# Irregular block faces remain economical separate meshes.
for side in [-1,1]:
    for j in range(4):
        B(fire,f'jamb_{side}_{j}',(.24,.31,.30),(fx+side*.79,fy-.13,.18+j*.30),
          (.40+random.uniform(-.035,.035),.385,.31))
B(fire,'lintel',(1.86,.34,.25),(fx,fy-.13,1.36),(.43,.415,.345))
B(fire,'mantel top',(1.98,.38,.075),(fx,fy-.145,1.515),(.45,.435,.36))
# Shaped inner lip, around the dark firebox.
for side in [-1,1]:
    R(fire,f'inner upright_{side}',(fx+side*.64,fy-.315,.10),
      (fx+side*.64,fy-.315,1.08),.045,color=(.32,.30,.24))
    R(fire,f'arch shoulder_{side}',(fx+side*.64,fy-.315,1.08),
      (fx+side*.51,fy-.315,1.18),.045,color=(.32,.30,.24))
R(fire,'arch top',(fx-.51,fy-.315,1.18),(fx+.51,fy-.315,1.18),.043,color=(.32,.30,.24))
# Soot-darkened brick backing with staggered mortar lines.
for row in range(8):
    for col in range(5):
        xx=fx-.56+col*.255+(row%2)*.10
        if xx<fx+.61:
            c=random.choice([(.19,.18,.14),(.23,.21,.16),(.14,.135,.105)])
            B(fire,f'firebrick_{row}_{col}',(.235,.018,.102),(xx,fy-.083,.13+row*.119),c)
scene.include('fireplace',fire)

# Narrow white electric heater leaning inside the fireplace's right edge.
heater=Asset('portable radiator')
for i in range(9):
    xx=4.93+i*.035
    B(heater,f'fin_{i}',(.022,.10,.48),(xx,4.16,.34),(.72,.73,.66))
for i,z in enumerate([.12,.57]):
    B(heater,f'crossbar_{i}',(.33,.12,.025),(5.07,4.16,z),(.68,.69,.61))
heater.turn('y',-10)
scene.include('heater',heater)
bin=Asset('small black waste bin')
bin.include('body',rod(radius=.095,length=.29,center=(5.50,4.18,.18),color=(.065,.073,.065)))
scene.include('bin',bin)

# Small circular rear-wall fitting above the locker.
clock=Asset('wall disc')
clock.include('rim',rod(radius=.105,length=.023,center=(3.00,4.545,2.36),
                        axis='+y',color=(.47,.51,.43)))
clock.include('face',rod(radius=.089,length=.027,center=(3.00,4.528,2.36),
                         axis='+y',color=(.60,.65,.57)))
scene.include('wall fitting',clock)

# All primitive dimensions are positive; fillet radii are <= half the minimum
# dimension. Indexed keys are unique. Supports are constructed at floor height;
# no bind dependencies are needed, and each movable object has its own hierarchy.
realize(scene)

# Subtle procedural grain supplies worn boards without image textures.
for obj in bpy.data.objects:
    if obj.type!='MESH':
        continue
    ancestry=[]
    p=obj
    while p:
        ancestry.append(p.name.lower())
        p=p.parent
    labels=' '.join(ancestry)
    if 'plank_' in labels or 'oak locker' in labels or 'left stud' in labels or 'ceiling beam' in labels:
        if not obj.data.materials:
            continue
        mat=obj.data.materials[0].copy()
        obj.data.materials[0]=mat
        mat.use_nodes=True
        nt=mat.node_tree
        bs=nt.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
        base=bs.inputs['Base Color'].default_value[:]
        tex=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise')
        tex.inputs['Scale'].default_value=4
        tex.inputs['Detail'].default_value=3
        coord=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
        mapping=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeVectorMath')
        mapping.operation='MULTIPLY'
        mapping.inputs[1].default_value=(35,1.4,7)
        nt.links.new(coord.outputs['Generated'],mapping.inputs[0])
        nt.links.new(mapping.outputs[0],tex.inputs['Vector'])
        ramp=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position=.20
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color=tuple(v*.56 for v in base[:3])+(1,)
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position=.78
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color=tuple(min(v*1.4,1) for v in base[:3])+(1,)
        nt.links.new(tex.outputs['Fac'],ramp.inputs[0])
        nt.links.new(ramp.outputs[0],bs.inputs['Base Color'])
        bump=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBump')
        bump.inputs['Strength'].default_value=.19
        bump.inputs['Distance'].default_value=.018
        nt.links.new(tex.outputs['Fac'],bump.inputs['Height'])
        nt.links.new(bump.outputs[0],bs.inputs['Normal'])
        bs.inputs['Roughness'].default_value=.72
    elif 'bunk' in labels:
        for mat in obj.data.materials:
            mat.use_nodes=True
            bs=mat.node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
            rgba=bs.inputs['Base Color'].default_value
            if sum(rgba[:3])<.65:
                bs.inputs['Metallic'].default_value=.68
                bs.inputs['Roughness'].default_value=.33

set_view(position=(4.15,-5.7,1.73), target=(2.55,3.05,1.48),
         lens=33, sensor=36, shift=(0,0))
world=bpy.context.scene.world
if world is None:
    world=bpy.data.worlds.new('World')
    bpy.context.scene.world=world
world.use_nodes=True
world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[0].default_value=(.58,.62,.49,1)
world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[1].default_value=.33
area_emitter(position=(2.7,-3.2,3.0),power=1150,size=4.2,
             target=(1.8,1.6,.6),color=(.93,.96,1.0))
area_emitter(position=(4.4,1.8,2.7),power=220,size=3.0,
             target=(2.7,4.4,1.0),color=(1.0,.91,.68))
sc=bpy.context.scene
sc.render.engine='CYCLES'
sc.cycles.samples=32
sc.render.resolution_x=512
sc.render.resolution_y=341
sc.render.resolution_percentage=100
sc.view_settings.view_transform='AgX'
sc.view_settings.look='AgX - Medium High Contrast'
```

from sceneact import *
import bpy, math, random

random.seed(14)
scene = Scene('Historic dormitory')

# Observed inventory: two iron bunks at left, a cropped foreground bunk at
# right, paneled oak locker, stone fireplace, white heater, bin, wall disc,
# timber-framed plaster walls, ceiling beams and long wooden floorboards.
# Reference landmarks estimated by eye: main aisle post (145,200),
# locker (307,174), fireplace (401,192), right foreground post (477,170).
# Feedback observations: rear furniture appears smaller and lower, while
# the right foreground bunk covers too much of the fireplace.
# Hypothesis: camera depth and lateral viewing angle explain these together.
# Main correction family is camera pose/shift only; furniture stays intact.
# Expected effect: enlarge rear furnishings, lift their framing, strengthen
# foreground perspective and move the close right bunk toward the image edge.
wood = (.25,.125,.052)
iron = (.085,.105,.102)
linen = (.88,.89,.84)
plaster = (.66,.66,.38)

def B(parent, key, size, center, color):
    return parent.include(key, box(size=size, center=center, color=color))

def R(parent, key, start, end, radius=.022, color=iron):
    return parent.include(key, rod(radius=radius, start=start, end=end, color=color))

for i in range(25):

           .155+random.random()*.045,
           .073+random.random()*.025)
        B(room,f'plank_{i}_{j}',(.279,2.247,.035),(x,y,.003),c)
B(room,'left plaster',(.13,8.7,3.05),(-.14,.65,1.525),(.67,.67,.49))
B(room,'rear plaster',(6.6,.15,3.05),(3.1,4.65,1.525),plaster)
B(room,'ceiling',(6.8,8.8,.13),(3.0,.6,3.09),(.66,.68,.47))
for i,y in enumerate([-3.0,-.8,1.5,3.65,4.52]):
    B(room,f'left stud_{i}',(.17,.16,3.03),(-.025,y,1.51),(.16,.12,.065))
for i,z in enumerate([.14,1.05,2.23,2.95]):
    B(room,f'left horizontal_{i}',(.17,8.7,.13),(-.015,.65,z),(.17,.125,.062))
for i,y in enumerate([-.5,3.4]):
    B(room,f'ceiling beam_{i}',(6.6,.22,.23),(3.0,y,2.98),(.12,.095,.046))
scene.include('architecture',room)

# Bunk builder maps frames, upholstery, ladder and attachments to one hierarchy.
def bunk(name,x,y,length=2.13,width=.94):
    a=Asset(name)
    for i,xx in enumerate([x-length/2,x+length/2]):
        for j,yy in enumerate([y-width/2,y+width/2]):
            R(a,f'post_{i}_{j}',(xx,yy,.06),(xx,yy,2.13),.027)
            a.include(f'cap_{i}_{j}',
                      ball(radius=.033,center=(xx,yy,2.135),color=iron))
            B(a,f'foot_{i}_{j}',(.105,.105,.035),(xx,yy,.045),(.21,.22,.19))
    for k,z in enumerate([.46,1.59]):
        B(a,f'bed base_{k}',(length+.025,width,.075),(x,y,z),iron)
        a.include(f'mattress_{k}',
                  fillet_box(size=(length-.035,width-.055,.16),radius=.065,
                             center=(x,y,z+.115),color=linen))
        B(a,f'sheet edge_{k}',(length-.015,width+.018,.052),
          (x,y,z+.13),(.91,.92,.88))
        a.include(f'duvet_{k}',
                  fillet_box(size=(length*.68,width-.045,.085),radius=.035,
                             center=(x+.27,y,z+.223),color=(.87,.89,.86)))
        a.include(f'pillow_{k}',
                  fillet_box(size=(.47,width*.77,.13),radius=.055,
                             center=(x-length*.35,y,z+.255),color=(.96,.95,.89)))
        for j,yy in enumerate([y-width/2,y+width/2]):
            heights=[z+.34,z+.49] if k==1 else [z+.23]
            for n,zz in enumerate(heights):
                R(a,f'side rail_{k}_{j}_{n}',
                  (x-length/2,yy,zz),(x+length/2,yy,zz),.018)
        for j,xx in enumerate([x-length/2,x+length/2]):
            for n,zz in enumerate([z+.31,z+.48]):
                R(a,f'end rail_{k}_{j}_{n}',
                  (xx,y-width/2,zz),(xx,y+width/2,zz),.019)
    lx=x+length/2+.025
    for i,yy in enumerate([y-width*.35,y+width*.35]):
        R(a,f'ladder upright_{i}',(lx,yy,.13),(lx,yy,1.98),.021)
    for i in range(6):
        zz=.32+i*.27
        R(a,f'ladder rung_{i}',(lx,y-width*.35,zz),(lx,y+width*.35,zz),.018)
    B(a,'number plaque',(.11,.025,.17),
      (x+length/2-.08,y-width/2-.022,2.08),(.12,.15,.13))
    return a

scene.include('front left bunk',bunk('front left bunk',1.00,.15))
scene.include('rear left bunk',bunk('rear left bunk',1.00,2.28))
right=bunk('cropped right bunk',5.05,-1.52,length=2.15,width=.97)

scene.include('cropped right bunk',right)

B(cab,'dark interior',(.92,.09,1.78),(cx,cy+.19,.99),(.105,.063,.025))
for i,x in enumerate([cx-.47,cx+.47]):

B(cab,'divider',(.045,.43,1.76),(cx+.005,cy,.99),(.33,.18,.063))
for i,z in enumerate([.11,.83,1.88]):
    B(cab,f'shelf_{i}',(.97,.52,.065),(cx,cy,z),(.31,.16,.049))
B(cab,'cornice',(1.08,.59,.075),(cx,cy,1.94),(.37,.21,.085))
B(cab,'cornice lip',(1.13,.62,.035),(cx,cy,1.987),(.28,.15,.052))
B(cab,'closed door',(.43,.055,1.70),(cx-.235,cy-.26,.99),(.38,.21,.078))
for i,z in enumerate([.50,1.34]):
    B(cab,f'recessed panel_{i}',(.33,.013,.64),
      (cx-.235,cy-.294,z),(.31,.155,.047))
    for j,xx in enumerate([cx-.416,cx-.055]):
        B(cab,f'panel stile_{i}_{j}',(.025,.025,.70),
          (xx,cy-.309,z),(.42,.24,.091))
    for j,zz in enumerate([z-.35,z+.35]):
        B(cab,f'panel rail_{i}_{j}',(.38,.025,.026),
          (cx-.235,cy-.309,zz),(.42,.24,.091))
for i,x in enumerate([cx-.37,cx+.37]):
    B(cab,f'foot_{i}',(.12,.38,.13),(x,cy,.065),(.24,.12,.036))
for i,z in enumerate([.52,1.30]):
    cab.include(f'door knob_{i}',
                ball(radius=.018,center=(cx-.08,cy-.335,z),color=(.12,.11,.06)))
for i,x in enumerate([cx+.10,cx+.23,cx+.36]):
    R(cab,f'hook_{i}',(x,cy+.09,1.74),(x,cy-.015,1.69),.012,(.12,.11,.08))
scene.include('locker',cab)

# Fireplace maps to masonry surround, hearth and soot-darkened brick backing.
fire=Asset('stone fireplace')
fx,fy=4.49,4.505
B(fire,'black opening',(1.36,.055,1.17),(fx,fy-.045,.59),(.075,.066,.049))
B(fire,'hearth slab',(1.97,.90,.07),(fx,4.22,.047),(.30,.28,.22))
for side in [-1,1]:
    for j in range(4):
        B(fire,f'jamb_{side}_{j}',(.24,.31,.30),
          (fx+side*.79,fy-.13,.18+j*.30),
          (.40+random.uniform(-.035,.035),.385,.31))
B(fire,'lintel',(1.86,.34,.25),(fx,fy-.13,1.36),(.43,.415,.345))
B(fire,'mantel top',(1.98,.38,.075),(fx,fy-.145,1.515),(.45,.435,.36))
for side in [-1,1]:
    R(fire,f'inner upright_{side}',
      (fx+side*.64,fy-.315,.10),(fx+side*.64,fy-.315,1.08),
      .045,(.32,.30,.24))
    R(fire,f'arch shoulder_{side}',
      (fx+side*.64,fy-.315,1.08),(fx+side*.51,fy-.315,1.18),
      .045,(.32,.30,.24))
R(fire,'arch top',(fx-.51,fy-.315,1.18),(fx+.51,fy-.315,1.18),
  .043,(.32,.30,.24))
for row in range(8):
    for col in range(5):
        xx=fx-.56+col*.255+(row%2)*.10
        if xx<fx+.61:
            c=random.choice([(.19,.18,.14),(.23,.21,.16),(.14,.135,.105)])
            B(fire,f'firebrick_{row}_{col}',(.235,.018,.102),
              (xx,fy-.083,.13+row*.119),c)
scene.include('fireplace',fire)

heater=Asset('portable radiator')
for i in range(9):
    B(heater,f'fin_{i}',(.022,.10,.48),(4.93+i*.035,4.16,.34),(.72,.73,.66))
for i,z in enumerate([.12,.57]):
    B(heater,f'crossbar_{i}',(.33,.12,.025),(5.07,4.16,z),(.68,.69,.61))
heater.turn('y',-10)
scene.include('heater',heater)

bin_asset=Asset('small black waste bin')
bin_asset.include('body',
                  rod(radius=.095,length=.29,center=(5.50,4.18,.18),
                      color=(.065,.073,.065)))
scene.include('bin',bin_asset)

disc.include('face',rod(radius=.089,length=.027,center=(3,4.528,2.36),
                        axis='+y',color=(.60,.65,.57)))
scene.include('wall fitting',disc)

    if any(s in labels for s in ['plank_','oak locker','left stud','ceiling beam']):

        mat=obj.data.materials[0].copy()
        obj.data.materials[0]=mat

        nt=mat.node_tree
        bs=nt.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
        base=bs.inputs['Base Color'].default_value[:]
        tex=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise')
        tex.inputs['Scale'].default_value=4
        tex.inputs['Detail'].default_value=3
        coord=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
        mapping=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeVectorMath')
        mapping.operation='MULTIPLY'
        mapping.inputs[1].default_value=(35,1.4,7)
        nt.links.new(coord.outputs['Generated'],mapping.inputs[0])
        nt.links.new(mapping.outputs[0],tex.inputs['Vector'])
        ramp=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position=.20
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color=tuple(v*.56 for v in base[:3])+(1,)
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position=.78
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color=tuple(min(v*1.4,1) for v in base[:3])+(1,)
        nt.links.new(tex.outputs['Fac'],ramp.inputs[0])
        nt.links.new(ramp.outputs[0],bs.inputs['Base Color'])
        bump=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBump')
        bump.inputs['Strength'].default_value=.19
        bump.inputs['Distance'].default_value=.018
        nt.links.new(tex.outputs['Fac'],bump.inputs['Height'])
        nt.links.new(bump.outputs[0],bs.inputs['Normal'])
